<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="טבת_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518916210_theRebbe_473" batchId="meluket-_D7_98_D7_91_D7_AA_meluket__BH_POST_1766518916210_theRebbe_473__p003">
  <section v="6">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The aspect of Levi, meaning "my husband will be joined to me," relates to the recitation of "Emes VeYatziv" after Shema, which refers to the Torah, through which this union is achieved.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the aspect of Levi, on the name "my husband will be joined to me,"</t>
    <t s="1">is that which after Shema we say "Emes VeYatziv" etc. "this matter is upon us,"</t>
    <t s="2">"this matter" refers to the Torah,</t>
    <t s="3">for through the Torah it becomes "my husband will be joined to me"</t>
    <t s="4">(as will be explained below).</t>
  </section>
  <section v="7">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The three aspects of Reuven, Shimon, and Levi correspond to the three lines of Torah, service, and acts of kindness, which are the foundations of the world and man.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">3)</t>
    <t s="1">And the explanation of the matter:</t>
    <t s="2">Behold, the three aforementioned aspects</t>
    <t s="3">(Reuven, Shimon, and Levi)</t>
    <t s="4">are the three lines upon which the world stands</t>
    <t s="5">[also, "the world is a small man,"</t>
    <t s="6">"you are called man"]</t>
    <t s="7">Torah, service, and acts of kindness.</t>
    <t s="8">The aspect of Reuven</t>
    <t s="9">(love)</t>
    <t s="10">is the line of acts of kindness.</t>
    <t s="11">For when one has love of Hashem, he also has love of Israel</t>
    <t s="12">[since love of Hashem and love of Israel are entirely one],</t>
    <t s="13">and therefore,</t>
    <t s="14">his service is in the line of acts of kindness,</t>
    <t s="15">for love is</t>
    <t s="16">the cause of kindness and its innerness,</t>
    <t s="17">a drawing down from above to below.</t>
    <t s="18">And the aspect of Shimon</t>
    <t s="19">(awe)</t>
    <t s="20">is the line of service,</t>
    <t s="21">the matter of prayer,</t>
    <t s="22">the left line</t>
    <t s="23">[and in prayer itself, this is the matter of the second portion of Shema,</t>
    <t s="24">as above],</t>
    <t s="25">an elevation from below to above.</t>
    <t s="26">And the aspect of Levi, on the name "my husband will be joined to me," is the line of Torah,</t>
    <t s="27">for through the Torah, Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one.</t>
    <t s="28">And this is the matter of "my husband will be joined to me,"</t>
    <t s="29">for through the Torah, a connection is made with "my husband," this is the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="30">until Israel and the Holy One, blessed be He, are entirely one.</t>
    <t s="31">And this is that the aspect of Levi is the matter of "Emes VeYatziv" etc. "this matter" that refers</t>
    <t s="32">(as above)</t>
    <t s="33">to the Torah.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="8">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>The service of Reuven, Shimon, and Levi (the two portions of Shema and Emes VeYatziv) is a preparation for the aspect of Yehudah, which is the service of the silent prayer, representing total self-nullification, akin to the crown of a good name that rises above the three crowns.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">4)</t>
    <t s="1">And this is "Yehudah, you, your brothers will praise you,"</t>
    <t s="2">that the service of the aspects of</t>
    <t s="3">(your brothers)</t>
    <t s="4">Reuven, Shimon, and Levi,</t>
    <t s="5">the two portions of Shema and Emes VeYatziv,</t>
    <t s="6">is an introduction and preparation for the aspect of Yehudah,</t>
    <t s="7">the service of the silent prayer,</t>
    <t s="8">thanksgiving and self-nullification,</t>
    <t s="9">like a servant before his master.</t>
    <t s="10">For the self-nullification of the silent prayer is a self-nullification in the ultimate sense, higher even than the self-nullification of Shema.</t>
    <t s="11">And this is also understood from the differences in the laws</t>
    <t s="12">(regarding interruption, etc.)</t>
    <t s="13">between Shema and the silent prayer.</t>
    <t s="14">And this matter</t>
    <t s="15">[that through the service of the aspects of Reuven, Shimon, and Levi, one subsequently reaches the aspect of Yehudah</t>
    <t s="16">(the fourth son)]</t>
    <t s="17">is in the manner of the known concept</t>
    <t s="18">regarding the three crowns</t>
    <t s="19">[the crown of Torah, the crown of priesthood, and the crown of kingship,</t>
    <t s="20">which are in the three lines of Torah, service, and acts of kindness]</t>
    <t s="21">and the crown of a good name that rises above them</t>
    <t s="22">[which is higher than them],</t>
    <t s="23">that in order to reach the aspect of the crown of a good name, it is through the three crowns,</t>
    <t s="24">it rises above them.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
